vignette: Dr. Everett Thompson's eyes still widened in fear when he recalled the day a bomb exploded at the bus station near his hospital. He had been on his way to work that morning, just like any other. The blast threw him off balance, and as he struggled to make sense of the chaos, he was hit with the sounds of screams and shattering glass. Even now, when he rode the bus to visit patients in outlying clinics, those same sounds echoed in his mind, transporting him back to that terrifying moment. Everett's wife, Sarah, had grown increasingly concerned about his mood swings and irritability. He would lash out at her for no reason, and even small noises around the house made him jump. "What's wrong with you?" she'd ask, but Everett couldn't explain. All he knew was that ever since the bombing, the world seemed a more menacing place. Every stranger on the bus looked like a potential threat; every creak in their old house sounded like an intruder. Being a doctor had always given Everett a sense of control and purpose, but now even his work felt precarious. He began to doubt his own abilities, wondering if he could truly keep his patients safe. His colleagues noticed the change too - how he would freeze during emergency drills or snap at nurses who didn't follow procedures exactly as written. "It's just protocol," they'd say, but for Everett, it was a matter of life and death. Everett felt like his whole life had been destroyed by that one event. He became withdrawn, avoiding social gatherings and public events, especially those involving large crowds or transportation hubs. Sarah tried to reassure him, but he couldn't shake the feeling that people were hiding something from him - that every smile concealed a sinister intention. Even her attempts at comfort felt insincere. As time passed, Everett's hypervigilance only intensified. He started listening for suspicious noises around his house, even when Sarah was home with him. "What are you doing?" she'd ask as he checked the locks for the umpteenth time that evening. "I just want to be safe," he'd reply, but deep down, he knew it wasn't just about safety - it was about a desperate attempt to regain some semblance of control over his shattered world. It was during one particularly intense episode, as he stood frozen in their living room, listening for the sound of footsteps outside, that Everett realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this - trapped in a never-ending cycle of fear and mistrust. The doctor who had always prided himself on being in control finally broke down, tears streaming down his face as he called Sarah over to hold him. "I'm scared," he whispered, the words barely audible. "I just want my life back." It was then that Everett knew he needed to confront the demons that haunted him - to learn how to quiet the constant threats in his mind and trust the world again. But for now, as he sat in their darkened living room, surrounded by shadows, all he could do was wonder: would it be too late?
